When converting decimal prices to whole cents, multiplying floating-point

of 3995. This made prices like 39.95 fail validation. Use Math.round() after

claude.result:
The fix is complete! I found and fixed the floating-point precision bug in three places:

1. **`src/money.js` line 13** (`parseEuros`): When parsing "39.95", multiplying by 100 was giving 3995.0000000000005 instead of 3995.
2. **`src/money.js` line 25** (`cellCents`): Same issue for imported prices.
3. **`src/locale.js` line 18** (`decimalCommaToCents`): Same issue for European-format decimals like "39,95".

The solution is to wrap the multiplication by 100 with `Math.round()` to ensure exact integer results. I've tested that Gym (39.95), Netflix (12.99), and Spotify (10.99) all work correctly now.

Ready to commit when you approve the git operations.
